## Motivation This PR validates ConvRot INT8 (`--quantization convrot_int8`) for: - Wan2.2 (T2V-A14B and I2V-A14B) - Wan-Animate-2 14B (base and distilled) Measured speed, memory and quality on GB200 and H100 for all four, plus two smoke cases for Wan2.2 in the B200 1-GPU suite (no CI case for Wan-Animate-2). TL;DR (ConvRot INT8 against BF16, same seed and same layout; see below for more details): - Recipe: `--quantization convrot_int8 --quantization-ignored-layers proj_out` on the stock BF16 checkpoints. No calibration data, no quantized checkpoint, no code change; the quantization page lists no other quantized path for I2V-A14B. - Wan2.2 T2V and I2V on GB200 (832x480, 81 frames, 30 steps): 1.17x at 1 GPU, 1.17x to 1.19x at 2 and 4 GPUs; 1.23x (T2V) and 1.20x (I2V) on one H100 NVL 94 GB. - Peak VRAM at 1 GPU reduced from 87.5 to 60.6 GiB (T2V) and from 88.1 to 61.8 GiB (I2V); about 27 GiB less per GPU at every layout. - Same-seed PSNR to BF16: 21.4 dB (T2V) and 28.1 dB (I2V) at 1 GPU. For scale, BF16 against itself moves by 24.0 to 24.8 dB (T2V) and 28.2 to 29.9 dB (I2V) when only the parallel layout changes, so ConvRot sits below that spread on T2V (by 0.6 to 3.4 dB across the 1-, 2- and 4-GPU layouts) and at its lower edge on I2V, 10 dB or more above the two-seed floor. - Wan-Animate-2 base: 1.07x and peak VRAM from 86.5 to 71.9 GiB at 1 GPU, 29.4 dB; distilled: 1.07x / 1.06x / 1.04x at 1 / 2 / 4 GPUs, peak VRAM from 65.3 to 50.7 GiB at 1 GPU, 33.9 dB. Why: - Wan2.2 I2V-A14B has no published ModelOpt FP8/NVFP4 transformer (the validated ModelOpt transformers on the quantization page cover T2V-A14B only), and producing one needs a calibration set of first-frame/prompt pairs; ConvRot INT8 is data-free and works on the stock checkpoint. - For T2V-A14B it is an alternative to the ModelOpt FP8 transformer with no conversion step and no extra artifact. - `convrot_int8` already runs on these models, but the quantization page scopes its quality claims to an explicit list (MiniMax-H3, Qwen-Image, Qwen-Image-Edit); this PR extends that list with the same kind of evidence the existing entries have, smoke-tested in CI and quality-validated offline. Based on main as of 2026-10-22 (`24e45961c6`), which includes #44085, the native support for the distilled Wan-Animate-2 checkpoint. ## Modifications ### New All six are edits of existing files (no new file); the first three are under `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/`. - `gpu_cases.py`: `ONE_GPU_CONVROT_INT8_CASES` = `wan22_convrot_int8_t2v` (`Wan-AI/Wan2.2-T2V-A14B-Diffusers`, `MODELOPT_T2V_CI_sampling_params`) and `wan22_convrot_int8_i2v` (`Wan-AI/Wan2.2-I2V-A14B-Diffusers`, `CONVROT_INT8_I2V_CI_sampling_params`), built with `_make_modelopt_ci_case` and `extras=["--quantization", "convrot_int8", "--quantization-ignored-layers", "proj_out"]`; appended to `ONE_GPU_B200_CASES`, empty on ROCm. - `testcase_configs.py`: `CONVROT_INT8_I2V_CI_sampling_params`, the `TI2V_sampling_params` prompt and image at 17 frames, 12 steps, seed 0, `output_size="496x496"` (what Wan I2V returns for the square CI image at the T2V smoke's 640x384 budget). - `perf_baselines/b200.json`: one entry per case with the siblings' eleven keys plus `timing_tolerance` 1.5, generated on a GB200 and NOT on a B200: placeholders to regenerate on the first B200 CI run (`SGLANG_GEN_BASELINE=1`). Once numbers from the B200 are available the tolerance can be dropped. - `docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/quantization.mdx`: the three models in the `convrot_int8` option row and the Warning list; six rows in the measured table (its intro now says these rows keep `proj_out` in BF16); one Wan2.2 paragraph and one Wan-Animate-2 sentence linking the cookbook sections. - `docs/cookbook/diffusion/Wan/Wan2.2.mdx`: new "4.2.4 ConvRot INT8 Quantization" (recipe, T2V and I2V commands, protocol, GB200 1/2/4-GPU table, quality and H100 NVL figures, four notes) and one bullet in "3.2 Configuration Tips". - `docs/cookbook/diffusion/Wan/Wan-Animate-2.mdx`: one row in each "3.3 Multi-GPU and memory presets" table and new "4.4 ConvRot INT8 quantization" (recipe, `sglang serve` command, per checkpoint a protocol, GB200 table and quality sentence, the 7-clip figures, hardware note). ### Shared code touched None: no change to the quantization configs, kernels or loaders. ### Supported features - The recipe `--quantization convrot_int8 --quantization-ignored-layers proj_out` on the stock checkpoints `Wan-AI/Wan2.2-T2V-A14B-Diffusers`, `Wan-AI/Wan2.2-I2V-A14B-Diffusers`, `Wan-AI/Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B-Diffusers` and `Wan-AI/Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B-Distilled-Diffusers`; no behaviour change. - Layouts measured: 1 GPU; 2 GPUs `--enable-cfg-parallel`; 4 GPUs `--enable-cfg-parallel --ulysses-degree 2` (Wan2.2 and Animate-2 base); `--ulysses-degree 2` / `4` (Animate-2 distilled, which rejects CFG parallelism). CFG-parallel and Ulysses replicate the DiT on every rank, so the per-GPU memory saving carries over. - Both backends stay selectable (`SGLANG_DIFFUSION_CONVROT_INT8_BACKEND`); every number here is the `jit` backend (number of quantized layers: `jit 400, comfy_kitchen 0` per expert in every Wan2.2 load log, `jit 480, comfy_kitchen 0` on Animate-2). ### Notes on model-specific parameters - Both A14B experts (`transformer`, `transformer_2`) are quantized at load, 400 of the 401 eligible linears each (26.17 -> 13.09 GiB per expert). Wan-Animate-2 has one expert, 480 of 481 linears (30.08 -> 15.04 GiB), so its per-GPU saving is about 15 GiB instead of the A14B's 27 GiB. - `--quantization-ignored-layers proj_out` keeps the output head in BF16 (it matches module paths in both experts); on the hardest T2V prompts this adds 2 to 4 dB (dancer 21.0 -> 24.6 dB, night street 17.0 -> 18.9 dB) at no measurable cost in speed or memory, so the docs recommend it on every layout. - The fused INT8 kernels JIT-compile once per machine (about 50 s on CC 10.0, 96 s on CC 9.0; needs nvcc) and run on CC 9.0 (H100/H200), 10.0 (B200/GB200) and 12.0 / 12.1 (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, RTX 50 series, DGX Spark); with a warm cache ConvRot loads in BF16's time, and the load peak (BF16 weights staged on the GPU before quantization) stays below the runtime peak. ### Rejected at startup - CC 10.3 (B300 / GB300) is refused by the JIT backend by design (`REFUSED_CAPABILITY_REASONS` in `convrot_int8_jit.py`: Blackwell Ultra's INT8 tensor-core rate makes W8A8 a slowdown); with `auto` the config then resolves to the `comfy-kitchen` INT8 kernels when installed (0.86x on MiniMax-H3) and otherwise fails with the install hint. The cookbooks say so; there T2V-A14B has the ModelOpt FP8/NVFP4 transformers and I2V-A14B no validated quantized path. - If the JIT probe sees no CUDA device at load (observed once as a host transient), `auto` falls back to `comfy_kitchen` the same way; `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_CONVROT_INT8_BACKEND=jit` turns that into an explicit error. ## Accuracy Tests Protocol: same seed, same prompt, ConvRot INT8 against the BF16 video of the same GPU layout; PSNR and SSIM over all frames, LPIPS (AlexNet) on every fourth frame; sharpness is the Laplacian variance and flicker the mean frame-to-frame pixel difference, both quoted as the ConvRot / BF16 ratio. Wan2.2: 832x480, 81 frames, 30 steps, CFG 5, seed 42, default negative prompt, one warmup plus six measured requests (one per prompt) per cell. Wan-Animate-2: `size` 640x800, `clip_len` 37, audio off; base checkpoint 40 steps, CFG 3; distilled checkpoint 10 steps, guidance 1.0 (DPM-Solver++ 2M, `log_scale` -1.3) on the native support merged in #44085. On every build used here the pipeline is bit-exact across reruns, GPU slots and nodes (BF16 vs BF16 and ConvRot vs ConvRot: PSNR inf, SSIM 1.000), so each row is a single number with no run-to-run band. ### Wan2.2 (T2V and I2V) Inputs: six T2V prompts and six I2V first-frame/prompt pairs built on four landscape stills (lake, waterfall, meadow, sea cliffs; two of them reused with a second prompt), supplied with this PR as the uploads below. Wan I2V keeps the first frame's aspect ratio inside the 832x480 budget, so the I2V outputs are 832x464 (lake), 464x832 (waterfall), 624x624 (meadow) and 960x400 (sea cliffs).

How to run: ```bash # GPU CI cases (B200 suite; smoke: load + generate, perf and consistency checks off) pytest -s python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/test_server_b200.py -k wan22_convrot_int8 # Generate sglang generate --model-path Wan-AI/Wan2.2-T2V-A14B-Diffusers \ --quantization convrot_int8 --quantization-ignored-layers proj_out \ --prompt "A curious raccoon" --save-output sglang generate --model-path Wan-AI/Wan2.2-I2V-A14B-Diffusers \ --quantization convrot_int8 --quantization-ignored-layers proj_out \ --image-path /path/to/first_frame.jpg --prompt "..." --save-output # Serve Wan-Animate-2 sglang serve --model-path Wan-AI/Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B-Diffusers \ --quantization convrot_int8 --quantization-ignored-layers proj_out --port 30010 ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Protocol: 1, 2 and 4 GPUs of 4x GB200 nodes (189 GB per GPU) and one H100 NVL 94 GB (PCIe, 310 W power cap, aarch64 host); sglang main `c5bf3aaf` (the distilled Animate-2 rows on the #44085 head) with torch 2.15.0a0 (pre-release build), CUDA 13.5, cuDNN 9.27 and the default `dynamic_cudnn_sdpa` attention backend (CUDA 13.0 driver on the H100 node); the accuracy rows above come from the same stack. E2E is the mean of the measured requests after one warmup, loading excluded; peak is the sglang runtime peak per GPU. The 1- and 2-GPU rows are same-time BF16/ConvRot pairs averaged over two rounds with the GPU slots swapped (slots on one tray differ by about 10 percent for the same cell, so a single un-swapped pair can read anywhere from 1.07x to 1.29x at 1 GPU); the 4-GPU rows are BF16 then ConvRot, two rounds. Outputs were bit-identical across rounds, GPU slots and nodes. ## Motivation This PR validates ConvRot INT8 (`--quantization convrot_int8`) for: - Wan2.2 (T2V-A14B and I2V-A14B) - Wan-Animate-2 14B (base and distilled) Measured speed, memory and quality on GB200 and H100 for all four, plus two smoke cases for Wan2.2 in the B200 1-GPU suite (no CI case for Wan-Animate-2). TL;DR (ConvRot INT8 against BF16, same seed and same layout; see below for more details): - Recipe: `--quantization convrot_int8 --quantization-ignored-layers proj_out` on the stock BF16 checkpoints. No calibration data, no quantized checkpoint, no code change; the quantization page lists no other quantized path for I2V-A14B. - Wan2.2 T2V and I2V on GB200 (832x480, 81 frames, 30 steps): 1.17x at 1 GPU, 1.17x to 1.19x at 2 and 4 GPUs; 1.23x (T2V) and 1.20x (I2V) on one H100 NVL 94 GB. - Peak VRAM at 1 GPU reduced from 87.5 to 60.6 GiB (T2V) and from 88.1 to 61.8 GiB (I2V); about 27 GiB less per GPU at every layout. - Same-seed PSNR to BF16: 21.4 dB (T2V) and 28.1 dB (I2V) at 1 GPU. **Issue**

`expected_load_ms` here (35.3 s, and 35.8 s for `wan22_convrot_int8_i2v` at L341) comes from a warm GB200. `_validate_and_record` calls `validate_load` even with `run_perf_check=False`, so the limit is 35.3 s x 2.5 = 88 s.
